title: CounterStroke: Investigating Evolutionary Image Counterfactual Generation
affiliation: Biocomputing & Developmental Systems (BDS) group, Department of Computer Science and Information Systems, University of Limerick, Ireland
abstract: Counterfactual explanations help interpret image classifiers by asking what changes would alter a prediction. Existing methods typically rely on gradient-based pixel-space optimisation or generative modelling. We introduce CounterStroke, an evolutionary framework that evolves structured drawing programs over the image. Evaluated on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet-100, CounterStroke achieves 100% validity on all classification datasets (vs 81% GradCF and 52% CFProto on CIFAR), with substantially sparser edits. Aggregating successful phenotypes yields attribution maps competitive under SRG (MNIST 0.483, CIFAR 0.224). The same representation supports blank-canvas synthesis of classifier-sufficient evidence with no factual image.
contributions: Grammar-guided evolutionary sketch programs that produce valid, sparse, inspectable image counterfactuals.
Benchmarks on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet-100 against gradient, prototype, and generative methods, plus Deep-SCM (MorphoMNIST, CelebA).
Six phenotype-based attribution maps competitive under SRG on MNIST and CIFAR.
Blank-canvas synthesis of classifier-sufficient sketches from an empty image.
